headline: Ellerston initiates Lendlease as a classic turnaround, trading at steep discount to NTA with earnings set to inflect
reasoning: Lendlease has undergone a painful business simplification, exiting overseas construction and development in the UK, US and Europe to focus on Australian operations and a $48.7bn FUM global investment management business. The bulk of de-risking is considered complete and as ~$3.6bn of non-core Capital Release Unit funds are progressively divested, balance sheet leverage should reduce materially. A PGGM mandate modernisation partnership worth $1.1bn in Japan to acquire warehouses and offices signals continued growth in the Asian platform, which generates ~65% margin versus the platform average of ~40%. The stock trades at a massive discount to property peers and to its $5.85 underlying NTA, with an undemanding PE of 10.2x on FY27 consensus earnings. Catalysts include a flagged A$500m buyback conditional on gearing normalising and a running dividend yield of 4.0%.
quote: LLC has for a period embarked on a major, yet painful business simplification journey, writing down and exiting its overseas construction and development businesses (UK, US and Europe) to focus on its Australian operations, coupled with a global investment management (IM) business ($48.7bn of FUM). We believe it's a classic turnaround situation, whereby the bulk of the de-risking is complete and as a much leaner company, it is way past peak balance sheet distress. As its ~$3.6bn of mainly non-core Capital Release Unit funds are progressively divested, this will reduce balance sheet leverage (a major source of contention for investors). As this capital is more sensibly re-deployed under a re-invigorated board and new management team, this should drive stronger underlying earnings. Towards month end, LLC announced a $1.1b mandate modernization partnership with PGGM in Japan to acquire warehouses and offices, with the fund targeting Tokyo and Osaka. LLC will be coinvesting a minority 5% of the equity and we see this announcement as a positive, showing that the Asian platform still has growth prospects. When coupled with an undemanding PE of 10.2x on FY27 consensus earnings, we see the current share price as an attractive entry point. Earnings should in fact inflect from here, with management guiding to stronger Investments, Development and Construction earnings in H2 FY26 and into FY27 (off a relatively simpler, Australia-focused base). There also exists the strong prospect of capital management, as the company has flagged a A$500m buyback conditional on gearing normalising toward management's target, alongside a running dividend yield of 4.0%.

headline: Chester views Lendlease as a compelling turnaround with AUD8.00/share DCF valuation as restructure unlocks ~AUD1bn EBITDA earnings power
reasoning: Lendlease is implementing a significant restructuring via its Capital Release Unit, targeting divestment of >AUD4bn in non-core assets and exiting overseas construction businesses to focus on its core Australian market. Once restructuring is complete, Chester estimates proceeds could repay AUD1.8bn of debt, allocate AUD900m to Australian developments, invest over AUD1bn into Global Investments, and leave ~AUD900m in surplus capital distributable to shareholders. We believe this short-term focus is obscuring the earnings power of the business once capital has been redeployed, earnings have normalised, and the portfolio reaches a more stable operating profile. From our calculations, with reference to the charts below, we believe that with the proceeds to come from announced divestments and assuming LLC are able to divest the remaining CRU assets at book value, or a slight discount to there will be: AUD1.8bn used to repay debt and obtain the midpoint of targeted gearing levels; AUD900m extra allocated to Australian developments; Over AUD1bn invested into their Global Investments business; ~AUD900m in surplus capital that could be distributed to shareholders. We believe this capital could potentially generate LLC ~AUD1bn in EBITDA p.a. (~AUD600m in NPAT). While it has been a longer process than most in the market are willing to wait we believe patient capital will be rewarded over the next 12-18 months. This is a true turnaround story.

headline: Morningstar values Lendlease at $4.50 with 27% upside despite strategic reset execution risks and elevated gearing
reasoning: Morningstar has a fair value estimate of $4.50 per Lendlease security, with the current price trading approximately 27% below that level. The strategic reset begun in May 2024 involves selling a $4.5 billion capital release unit portfolio, but execution has been slower than expected, with roughly one quarter to one third of assets still unsold. A Milan development sale at a 60% discount to book value spooked the market and prompted Morningstar to slash its fair value estimate, though subsequent transactions in Australia and the UK at book value restored some confidence. Gearing sits at approximately 33%, well above management's 5-15% target, which is concerning for a developer with long-dated projects and uncertain cash flows. Morningstar now assumes a 50% discount to book value on the remaining ~$2 billion of capital release unit assets, and believes contracted sales of $1.5-1.6 billion plus additional core asset disposals of ~$1 billion should bring gearing back to target without requiring an equity raise. The key catalyst is continued asset sales at reasonable discounts within a reasonable timeframe, moving the narrative from 'bad to less bad'.
quote: So currently Morningstar values lend lease have $4.50 per security. Um, just last time I checked this morning, I think the security price is still 27% below our fair value estimate. The the transactions last week actually gave us a bit more confidence, gave us a clearer picture of how landlords can actually pay down its debt, reduce their gearing. They the management has a target gearing of 5 to 15%. And at the moment they're gearing it's about 33%, which isn't particularly high for companies in the real estate sector. But it is high for a developer with a lot of, um, long dated projects with high uncertainty in the timing of cash flows. So we would like to see gearing lower, and now they have contracted sales about 1.5 $1.6 billion. They are thinking of selling some assets in their core businesses, which are about another $1 billion. And also, let's not forget that they still have about a quarter assets left in the capital release unit, which is about another $2 billion. So all these combined should bring gearing back down to 15%, which is what the management is targeting now. So we think that they are unlikely to need to raise equity on that front.
episode_title: This REIT's strategic reset leaves investors wanting more

headline: Cooper Investors sees compelling Risk-Adjusted Value Latency in Lendlease as development returns recover and the stock trades near GFC trough valuations.
reasoning: Lendlease's development business has generated only ~4.4% ROIC over the past four years, well below its 10-13% through-the-cycle target, due to the COVID-related property cycle followed by monetary tightening. The stock is trading at ~0.75x last reported NTA, in line with GFC trough levels of ~0.8x. Cooper Investors sees a pathway to reversion in development returns as the cycle recovers. They also see potential for significant value creation in global real estate funds management given Lendlease's market presence, brand, and asset creation capability. A strategy update in May showed a step change in focus, with plans to simplify the organisational structure, exit international development and construction, and redeploy capital into the high-returning Australian development business and international investment management platform.
quote: The COVID-related property cycle of 2020/2021, which was followed almost immediately by the monetary tightening-induced cycle that we are currently experiencing, has seen Lendlease's development business generate a ~4.4% ROIC over the past four years. This is well below the 10-13% through-the-cycle target, a target that has been comfortably achieved historically. With a pathway towards reversion in development returns to more historical levels over the coming years as the cycle recovers, combined with the stock currently trading at ~0.75x last reported net tangible assets (in line with the trough of ~0.8x experienced during the GFC), we believe this opportunity represents compelling Risk-Adjusted Value Latency. In addition to the reversionary opportunity that underpins our investment proposition, we also see the potential for significant value creation in global real estate funds management given Lendlease's market presence, brand and asset creation capability. Having said that, successfully executing on this long-term opportunity is likely to require a significantly greater focus and intentionality than what Lendlease has displayed historically, along with cultural change. In this regard, it was pleasing to see a step change in focus, and intentionality from current Lendlease management at their strategy update in May.

headline: Tanarra Capital calls for new external Chair and board renewal at Lendlease to unlock value from strategic refocus on core Australian strengths
reasoning: Tanarra believes Lendlease's poor security price performance stems from undisciplined capital allocation and an overextension into too many geographies and business lines. Tanarra argues the company must refocus on these core strengths to deliver substantially better future performance. To achieve this, Tanarra expects Chair Michael Ullmer to retire at the November AGM after 13 years on the board, and calls for a new outside appointment with strong Australian property expertise as Chair. They argue good governance demands this Chair not be an existing board member, and that the new Chair should lead a broader board renewal process in close consultation with key investors. Tanarra is also critical of management retaining three investment banks to advise on the forthcoming investor day, viewing it as symptomatic of weak strategic leadership.
quote: Although Lendlease's security price performance in recent years has been very poor, the company does have fundamental strengths. It has a "moat" business in Australian construction where there is a shortage of qualified head contractors for major projects; it has a record of excellence in urban regeneration and mixed-use developments in Australia; and it has an emerging opportunity in growth sectors such as build-to-rent. We believe that refocusing the business on its core strengths should enable substantially better future performance. The era of Lendlease trying to be all things to all people in all parts of the world, with undisciplined capital allocation, must be at an end, now.

headline: Tanarra flags likely further impairments at Lendlease's Victoria Cross North Sydney office project as a major investor concern
reasoning: Tanarra highlights that Lendlease has earned a reputation for consistent below-the-line charges totalling $1.85bn over the last six years, excluded from STI executive compensation plans, which creates a market expectation of continued landmines. Specifically, Tanarra notes that many in financial and property markets believe further impairments are likely at the Victoria Cross office project in North Sydney, which remains only 6% leased despite nearing completion. They argue this pattern of 'death by a thousand cuts' through non-operating charges is a major impediment to investor interest and calls for conservative provisions to be taken now on questionable projects.
quote: Stop the 'death by a thousand cuts' by below-the-line 'non-operating and non-core' items every earnings result. Take conservative provisions now on questionable projects. Lendlease has unfortunately earned a reputation over time for consistent below-the-line charges, which are also excluded from STI executive compensation plans. These have been a feature of results every year for the last six years, now totaling $1.85bn. There is a market expectation this will continue, and represent another major impediment to investor interest – where and when will the next landmine go off? For example, many in the financial and property markets believe that further impairments are likely at the Victoria Cross office project in North Sydney, which is still only 6% leased despite nearing completion.

headline: Tanarra Capital urges Lendlease to pursue demerger, exit international construction and reset strategy to unlock securityholder value
reasoning: Tanarra Capital, as a long-term material shareholder of Lendlease for over two years, argues the company's global growth strategy has destroyed securityholder returns and calls for a comprehensive demerger analysis at the upcoming Investor Day on an 'if not, why not?' basis. They recommend Lendlease exit all international construction, which has generated only $171m in profits on $32.6bn in revenues since FY17, describing the business as simply unsustainable. Tanarra further calls for radical cost reduction, a cultural reset, and more ambitious mid-teens ROE targets, arguing that an 8-10% ROE target is inappropriate given Lendlease's risk profile when investors can earn the same in low-risk credit. They want the company to drop arbitrary FUM and development completion volume targets, exit long-dated high-risk projects like Euston Station UK, and radically improve financial transparency. Tanarra believes significant growth runway remains in Australia through Build to Rent, Mixed Use Urban Regeneration, Affordable Housing, and apartment supply, and expresses willingness to remain a long-term investor if strategic redirection occurs.
quote: We have arrived at these views after close evaluation from being a securityholder for over two years now. We are conveying the views solely as Tanarra, but are confident that many of the views expressed in this letter are widely shared in the equity market, as showed in the 2023 Remuneration Report vote. We are also writing this in the belief that Lendlease can once again be a company that not only builds beautiful buildings, but also generates great returns for its investors.

headline: Tanarra calls on Lendlease to exit Euston Station UK project as unsuitable for a mid-size public company's balance sheet
reasoning: Tanarra argues that very long-dated, high-risk and unpredictable projects such as Euston Station in the UK are inappropriate for Lendlease's balance sheet. The project has many inherently uncontrollable factors and is reliant on high theoretical long-dated end-values, with no cash flow expected for over a decade even if HS2 reaches the station — an outcome that is itself highly uncertain. Tanarra argues that irrespective of theoretical IRRs, such projects are a poor use of capital for a mid-size public company when direct and indirect people costs are also considered.
quote: A good step in this direction would be to exit very long dated, high-risk and unpredictable projects – e.g. Euston Station in the UK. These projects have many inherently uncontrollable factors and are reliant on high theoretical long-dated end-values to be successful. Euston won't start generating cash flow for over a decade even if HS2 ever reaches the station, which at this point is highly uncertain. Irrespective of theoretical IRRs, it's not a good use of a midsize public company's balance sheet, even before considering all the direct and indirect people costs involved.

headline: Cooper Investors maintains high conviction in Lendlease, citing cyclical reversion in the development business and improving operating trends in global gateway cities

quote: We continued to test our investment proposition in Lendlease (LLC) with company and other related meetings during our trips to both the US and Europe during the quarter. The core of our investment proposition revolves around a cyclical reversion in the development business which has seen completions fall from a peak of $5.6bn pre-pandemic (FY19) to a trough of $0.2bn in 1HFY22. Given that, it was pleasing to see the strength of residential apartment markets, particularly on the rental side with multiple local real estate agents describing activity levels as the best they have seen. Also evident was both the demand for and rarity of high quality, modern and sustainable office space post pandemic as distinct from older, higher emitting and less technology enabled product that today represents the majority of office stock in markets such as London. Being on the ground, observing these trends and the general "buzz" that is back in global gateway cities such as New York, London and Milan, increases our confidence that LLC's operating trends are now positive and supportive of moving the development pipeline into delivery. Combined, this reaffirms our conviction that LLC has the product, the market conditions and the capability to deliver ~$8bn in development completions from FY24 and represents an investment with compelling risk adjusted value latency.

headline: Seen as attractively valued with a superior earnings profile versus 2.5 years ago, supported by its urban regeneration pipeline and integrated business model.
reasoning: Greencape views Lend Lease as one of only three global players capable of competing in urban regeneration, with projects in Boston, Chicago, Singapore and Kuala Lumpur demonstrating strong execution. The integrated model allows Lend Lease to clip the ticket across design, construction, development and funds management, creating an efficient capital recycling loop. The funds management arm provides a willing buyer for Lend Lease product, liberating capital for the next project. Management is running an undergeared balance sheet (~5% gearing) despite long-term incentives that reward leverage, which Greencape views as shareholder-friendly and deserving of a re-rating. The stock currently trades on 12x P/E versus 15x the last time it was at the same share price 2.5 years ago, yet the earnings profile is arguably better given reduced gearing, completed apartment settlements, meaningful provisions raised, and a growing development pipeline and construction backlog. Lend Lease is also well positioned to grow its Australian infrastructure construction business given a strong pipeline of government-sponsored projects in Melbourne and Sydney.
quote: Whilst we won't go into the intricacies of our Lend lease valuation, we will mention that the last time Lend Lease traded at this share price (2.5 years ago), it attracted a price/earnings multiple of 15x vs the 12x it trades on today. It would be remiss of us not to point out that in that period they have reduced gearing, progressed through 2.5 years of apartment settlements, have raised a meaningful provision against future settlements (effectively de-risking them), whilst continuing to grow its Development Pipeline and Construction backlog. Therefore, we think today that the future earnings profile is arguably better than at any time over the past 10 years.
